# InterDigital and NHK Awarded IBC Best in Show for VVC Multilayer Coding


InterDigital and NHK earn an IBC 2026 Best in Show award for VVC Multilayer Coding, advancing efficient, flexible video delivery for broadcast and streaming.


September 2026


InterDigital Comms


[VVC](https://www.interdigital.com/blog?tags=VVC)[Video](https://www.interdigital.com/blog?tags=Video)[Video Codecs](https://www.interdigital.com/blog?tags=Video%20Codecs)


InterDigital and NHK (Japan Broadcasting Corporation), Japan’s public service media organization, were recognized with a “Best in Show” award for their demonstration of VVC Multilayer Coding at IBC 2026. VVC Multilayer Coding enables multiple versions of video content to be carried within a coordinated VVC bitstream, enabling broadcasters and streamers to more efficiently and flexibly deliver high-quality picture content.


The joint InterDigital - NHK demonstration showed two aspects of the VVC Multilayer Main 10 profile that enables greater personalization, picture quality, and efficiency in broadcast and streaming, and promotes its wider adoption in real-world services. This feature supports the efficient delivery of different or enhanced versions of the same content, bypassing the need to independently encode and distribute every resolution.


NHK demonstrated content personalisation enabled by VVC Multilayer and MPEG-H 3D audio coding, highlighting an ability to switch video and audio in a coordinated manner to empower richer user experiences. It shows how VVC enhancement layers can add overlays like captions, sign language, or reframed visuals while reusing a common base layer. By reframing the base layer and overlaying additional content in an enhancement layer, users can choose between viewing the base or an enhanced experience.


VVC Multilayer Coding can “skip” over unchanged areas while encoding only the content containing the additional content overlay. Instead of encoding each version independently, this offers a more efficient approach to creating multiple personalised compositions.


InterDigital demonstrated how VVC Multilayer Coding delivers improvements in picture quality and efficiency over independent encoding. Our research compares dual-layer with single-layer coding and upscaled base-layer codingto show how VVC enhancement layers can efficiently improve picture quality.


InterDigital’s contributions to scalability demonstrate how a VVC enhancement layer can deliver significant improvements in quality in broadcast and streaming applications, offering greater efficiency than independent encoding. In other words, VVC Multilayer Coding efficiently delivers the same content at different resolutions or quality levels.


Our approach first encodes a lower-resolution HD base layer, and then the enhancement layer uses inter-layer prediction to create a higher-quality UHD version from that base. VVC integrated reference picture resampling supports the required upscaling, downscaling, and reframing of the video content.


The result is compelling for broadcasters and streaming providers, who get the flexibility to support multiple resolutions without paying the bandwidth penalty of independently encoding and distributing each resolution. The bitrate for the combined HD base and UHD enhancement together is roughly the same as encoding UHD independently at comparable quality.


The efficiency benefits of these enhancements have been demonstrated through the MPEG VVC multilayer verification test, which found dual-layer coding significantly more efficient than simulcast, where each resolution is encoded independently. Supporting multiple resolutions from a coordinated bitstream, dual-layer VVC achieved performance on par with conventional single-layer high-resolution coding, while delivering better quality than simply upscaling the base layer. These results demonstrate that broadcasters and streaming providers can offer multiple resolutions and premium viewing experiences, without the significant bandwidth overheads associated with simulcast delivery for broadcasters, and storage requirements for streaming providers.


Ultimately, VVC Multilayer Coding enables broadcasters and streaming providers to flexibly and efficiently serve multiple resolutions from a coordinated bitstream, offering greater personalisation, with greater efficiency than simulcast for broadcast and saving storage for streaming providers.
